chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us from Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adami, from Mubarak the servant of al-Rida, from al-Rida Ali ibn Musa, peace be upon them both. He said:

A believer cannot be a true believer until he has three characteristics: a quality from his Lord, a quality from his Prophet, and a quality from his wali. As for the quality from his Lord, it is concealing his secret. Allah, exalted is His majesty, said: "He is the Knower of the Unseen, and He does not disclose His Unseen to anyone, except whom He is pleased with from among the messengers" [72:26-27]. As for the quality from his Prophet, it is being friendly with the people, for indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded His Prophet, blessings of Allah be upon him and his family, to be friendly with the people, and said: "Take to clemency, enjoin in established virtues, and turn away from the ignorant" [7:199]. As for the quality from his wali, it is patience during distress and affliction. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "And those who are patient during distress and affliction and at the time of tribulation -- these are the ones who have been sincere, and these are the Godfearing" [2:177].

key_terms.خصال: khisal -- characteristics or qualities; here referring to three essential traits of a true believer
key_terms.كتمان السر: kitman al-sirr -- concealing one's secret; a divine quality the believer should emulate
key_terms.مداراة: mudarah -- being friendly, courteous, and diplomatic with people; a key prophetic virtue

ai.seo_question: What are the three characteristics of a true believer according to Imam al-Rida from God, the Prophet, and the Imam?
ai.summary: Imam Ali al-Rida (AS) teaches that a true believer must embody three characteristics drawn from God, the Prophet, and the wali (Imam). From God: concealing secrets, as God conceals the Unseen (Quran 72:26). From the Prophet: being friendly with people, as Allah commanded the Prophet in Quran 7:199. From the wali: patience in distress and affliction, as described in Quran 2:177. This hadith, from the 52nd session of al-Saduq's Amali, establishes a tri-partite model of faith rooted in divine, prophetic, and Imamic examples.
